evidence.claim: From Lake Ontario through Adirondack communities to twice-Olympic Lake Placid
evidence.quote: Stretching from the Great Lake Ontario to legendary Lake Champlain, the Olympic Trail is packed with scenic and recreational attractions. One highlight of the trip is the Village of Lake Placid, which hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 1932 and 1980.

evidence.claim: The Olympic Trail connects Sackets Harbor and Keeseville over 170 miles, from the Lake Ontario region into the Adirondack Mountains.
evidence.quote: Length: 170 miles Region: Lake Ontario/Adirondack Mountains Connects: Sackets Harbor and Keeseville

evidence.claim: New York’s Department of Transportation identifies scenic and recreational themes for the byway, including places for hiking, camping, canoeing and fishing.
evidence.quote: Spots for Adirondack hiking, camping, canoeing, and fishing are abundant. The hamlets are charming and the scenery is stunning. Themes: Scenic, Recreational

evidence.claim: Cranberry Lake, Tupper Lake and Saranac Lake lie along the corridor to Lake Placid.
evidence.quote: Natural Bridge, Star Lake, Cranberry Lake, connects Ripley, NY on the PA border to Tupper Lake, Saranac Lake, Lake Placid and Massena. Parallels Lake Erie, the Niagara Wilmington.

evidence.claim: Railways carried both resort passengers and lumber through these mountains.
evidence.quote: Railroads both carried passenger traffic to the growing resort areas of the Adirondacks and shipped out the millions of feet of lumber that were harvested from this area into the early 20th century.

evidence.claim: The Delaware and Hudson reached Saranac Lake from Plattsburgh in 1887; five years later, the Mohawk and Malone reached nearby Lake Clear Junction.
evidence.quote: the Chateaugay branch of the Delaware and Hudson Railroad reached Saranac Lake from Plattsburgh in 1887. Five years later, the Mohawk and Malone Railway main line reached nearby Lake Clear Junction.

evidence.claim: Lake Placid hosted the Winter Olympics in 1932 and again in 1980.
evidence.quote: the Village of Lake Placid, which hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 1932 and 1980.

evidence.claim: From Sackets Harbor, the eastward journey reaches Natural Bridge at the western edge of the Adirondacks, then Harrisville.
evidence.quote: Natural Bridge is located on New York State Route 3 southeast of Fort Drum, at the western edge of the Adirondacks. Watertown, the Jefferson county seat, is 23 miles (37 km) to the southwest via Routes 3 and 3A, while Harrisville is 11 miles (18 km) to the northeast.

evidence.claim: Navy Point, now a marina for private boats, was the site of a wartime shipyard.
evidence.quote: Navy Point is a marina providing moorings and facilities for private boats.

evidence.claim: During the War of 1812, the U.S. Navy established its Great Lakes headquarters here, and more than 3,000 men worked at the yard.
evidence.quote: To support the War of 1812, the US Navy built a major shipyard and its headquarters for the Great Lakes at the village. Within a short period, more than 3,000 men worked at the shipyard.

evidence.claim: The Army built earthworks, forts and barracks to defend the village and the naval yard.
evidence.quote: The Army constructed earthworks, forts, barracks and supporting infrastructure to defend the village and navy shipyard

evidence.claim: By autumn 1814, Sackets Harbor ranked behind only Albany and New York City among the state’s population centers.
evidence.quote: By the fall of 1814, this was the third-largest population center in the entire state, after Albany and New York City.

evidence.claim: The war ended before the last warship, USS New Orleans, was finished. Stored unfinished, she was finally scrapped in 1883.
evidence.quote: The end of the war came in 1815 before the Navy completed construction of the last warship, the USS New Orleans. She was put into storage and never completed. She was finally scrapped in 1883.

evidence.claim: Main Street’s preserved nineteenth-century buildings form part of the village historic district.
evidence.quote: The heart of the village, with a Main Street and well-preserved 19th century buildings, has been recognized as the Sackets Harbor Village Historic District

evidence.claim: The Indian River runs underground through the marble cave that gave Natural Bridge its name.
evidence.quote: The name "Natural Bridge" was derived from Natural Bridge Caverns, marble cave which the Indian River runs underground through.

evidence.claim: The caverns once operated as a show cave, with visitors taken by boat along the underground river.
evidence.quote: Natural Bridge Caverns, the hamlet's namesake, was formerly operated as a show cave, with tourists being ferried by boat on the underground portion of the Indian River.

evidence.claim: Joseph Bonaparte, the former king of Spain, built a summer residence here in 1829 after inspecting his land the previous year.
evidence.quote: After coming to look at his land in 1828, he was impressed by the limestone arch and with being so close to his lake, "Lake Bonaparte" (8 miles (13 km) to the northeast), he decided to build a second summer residence in Natural Bridge in 1829.

evidence.claim: Saranac Lake’s cure cottages grew from a doctor’s search for relief from tuberculosis.
evidence.quote: In 1876, Dr. Edward Livingston Trudeau arrived from New York City to treat his tuberculosis (TB) by a stay in the mountains.

evidence.quote: The Trudeau Institute, an independent medical research center, developed from Trudeau's work for the sanitarium. In 1964, the Trudeau Institute began researching the functions of the immune system and how it guards against many infectious diseases, including tuberculosis.
